LESSON: READING 6.2.1 READING FLUENCY

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.2: Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is reading a text fluently important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a text at the right speed, accurately and with expression for effective communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 6.2.1 READING FLUENCY
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 6.2.1 READING FLUENCY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read a text at the right speed, accurately and with expression for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to read a text at the right speed, accurately and with expression for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read a text at the right speed, accurately and with expression for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read a text at the right speed, accurately and with expression for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read a text at the right speed, accurately and with expression for effective communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read a text at the right speed, accurately and with expression for effective communication.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is reading a text fluently important?
2. How can one read a text fluently?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read a text at the right speed, accurately and with expression for effective communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
